title: Community Health Worker
author: Dayone Koo
_comment: PROGRAM EVALUATION (evaluate-program skill). Subject is the PROGRAM (Foothill College x TOP 126100), not a job title. Destination SOCs DERIVED: crosswalk(126100) intersected with SECTORS['health'].socs minus ALL_OTHER/PROMOTION/EXPERIENCE_5YR = ['21-1094']. Dropped: 11-9111, 21-1091, 25-1071, 99-9999. Peer set = top 6 Bay colleges by 5-year awards on THIS TOP (a program evaluation's peers must share the TOP; the role report mixed TOPs). live_postings and competencies reused verbatim from the matching role report (same SOCs, already verified). EVIDENCE-FORWARD, NO VERDICT. EDITION 2026-09-18: crosswalk_chain true — the TOP–CIP–SOC Crosswalk section now argues the destinations; the demand note keeps only the COE sentence. DEMAND VINTAGE 2025–2030: demand figures re-read against the Centers of Excellence 2025–2030 release (2026-09-18 refresh).
lede: This evaluation assembles labor-market supply and demand evidence for Foothill College's Community Health Worker program (TOP 126100): regional demand for the occupations it leads to, its award and enrollment trends alongside other colleges offering the same program in the region, and how its courses align with the work of those occupations.
demand_note: [According to the Centers of Excellence](https://datastudio.google.com/u/0/reporting/c01114ab-6bc3-4529-bace-e933fe293b86/page/1v72D), Community Health Workers (SOC 21-1094) have roughly 370 openings a year in the Bay Area.
alignment_note: The colleges offering TOP 126100 in the Bay Area. Each supports SOC 21-1094 through the same TOP–CIP–SOC crosswalk.
award_note: Awards conferred each year by each college's program. An empty cell means DataMart reported no data.
enrollment_note: Enrollment each term in each college's program. An empty cell means DataMart reported no data.

21-1094.title: SLH Care Management Community Health Worker

21-1094.description: Promotes health within a community by helping residents adopt healthy behaviors and advocating for their needs with healthcare providers and social service agencies.

curriculum_note: O*NET maintains a set of detailed work activities that identify the competencies central to each job. Below, the Community Health Worker program's courses are mapped to the work activities of its destination occupation, based on how each course is described in its Course Outline of Record (COR).
chain_note: The Chancellor's Office classifies community health care worker programs as TOP 1261.00. Two federal codes carry it, and both resolve to one occupation, Community Health Workers.
